title: No audio in Teams meeting, the other side can't hear me
description: My microphone didn't work in 3 separate meetings today. The headset works fine in other apps on Windows.

worklogs.description: Checked Windows Privacy > Microphone settings, Teams was set to 'Allow'.
Cleared the Teams Modern Auth cache (%appdata%\Microsoft\Teams\Cache), user signed in again.
Device Manager: USB Audio driver showed as 'up to date'; ran an enumeration of the sound panel.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: I have a critical customer meeting at 2 PM right now, let's please find a quick fix.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Got it, I'm on it right away. First some quick checks: in Teams > Settings > Devices > Microphone, which device is selected? Does the 'Make a test call' button work?

comments.author: customer
comments.message: 'Headset Microphone (Jabra Evolve 65)' is selected. On the test call it says 'Hi, this is Test Call' but then it doesn't play my voice back — just silence.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: OK, that means the mic isn't reaching Teams. Could you unplug the headset from USB and plug it back in? Also, right-click the sound icon on the computer and in 'Sound settings > Input', I'd like to see whether the progress bar for the Jabra moves when you speak.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: I did the USB unplug-replug. In Sound settings the bar DOES RESPOND when I speak — so Windows hears it. But Teams doesn't.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Excellent diagnosis. The problem is specifically between Teams and the device. Let's go through these steps in order: 1) Fully close Teams (Task Manager → End Task the Teams process), 2) Open the %appdata%\Microsoft\Teams folder, 3) DELETE the 'Cache', 'GPUCache', and 'IndexedDB' subfolders (your app data won't be lost), 4) Reopen Teams. In my experience this method works 90% of the time.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: Did it! Teams reopened and on the test call it now hears my voice 🎉 I'll make the 2 PM meeting. Thank you so much.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Teams cache corruption — my 3rd case in the last month. I'll send a notification to the endpoint management team; these kinds of issues happen after a Teams auto-update. I'll get confirmation from the user after the meeting and resolve it.
